title: Cohomological smoothness of smooth morphisms
statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
for every smooth separated morphism $f:X\to Y$ of relative dimension
$d$ put

$$
\omega_f\;=\;Rf^!\Lambda_Y.
$$

Then:

1. *Tensor formula.* For every $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$ the
canonical map
$$
Lf^*K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}\omega_f\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rf^!K
$$
is an isomorphism.
1. *Invertibility.* $\omega_f$ is invertible.
1. *Base change.* The formation of $\omega_f$ and of the
canonical map is compatible with arbitrary base change: for a
Cartesian square with $f'$ the base change of $f$,
$$
Lu^*\omega_f\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\omega_{f'},
$$
and the two canonical maps correspond under $Lu^*$; this holds for
*arbitrary* $v$ by [lem-pur-smb-extraordinary].
1. *Composition.* The tensor formula is compatible with
composition of smooth morphisms, through the composition isomorphism
for $R^!$ of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image].

(*Orientation-free form*: none of the four statements identifies
$\omega_f$ with a twist and a shift; that identification,
$\omega_f\cong\Lambda(d)[2d]$, is the content of
[thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object] proved below from the diagonal
argument.)

proof.text: Work at the finite stage $A=\Lambda=A_{E,n}$, as specified by [def-pur-conventions]; the other coefficient stages are subsequent transports, not an extra assertion here. The schemes and base changes in this assertion are finite-type $k$-schemes. They are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], since a field is Noetherian. In particular they are quasi-compact and quasi-separated. The assumed separated finite-type $f$ has a compactification $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}Y$ by [thm-nagata-compactification]. Its proper part is finite type over $Y$, so $\overline X$ is finite type over $k$ and has finite dimension by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type]. Choose a nonnegative integer bounding that dimension (take zero for an empty compactification). The ring $A$ is finite by [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Also $|\ell|_E=\ell^{-1}<1$; writing $\ell=u\varpi_E^e$ by its uniformizer decomposition gives $e\geq1$, hence $\ell^n\in(\varpi_E^n)$ and $N=\ell^n$ annihilates $A$. This $N$ is invertible over $k$ because $\ell\ne p$. Thus the Noetherian, compactifiable, coefficient and pure-dimension hypotheses of [thm-asd-smooth-tensor] and the compactification-dimension hypothesis of [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] hold. The affine-space model also has the ordinary adjunction supplied by [cor-amb-affine-space-adjunction], and the historical affine-line supported Kummer normalization is uniquely characterized by [prop-pur-affine-line-orientation-uniqueness]; these record the historical model normalization while the argument below remains orientation-free. The same verification applies to $f'$ and to any other smooth map used below.

source.place: First paragraph: finite coefficient stage; hypotheses of the ordinary-etale input

proof.text:
Write $V_T=\nu_T^*$. Given $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$, [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin](ii) supplies a bounded constructible etale antecedent $H$ and $K\cong V_YH$. We need no Tor assertion about $H$ to apply the ordinary-etale tensor theorem, which allows every complex. By [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] the unit $H\to R\nu_{Y,*}V_YH$ is an isomorphism. Consequently the defining formula [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] gives
$$Rf^!K\cong V_Xf^\times H,\qquad \omega_f\cong V_XW_f,\quad W_f=f^\times A_Y.$$
Here $f^\times$ is the ordinary-etale compact-support right adjoint; it is not an unrestricted pro-etale adjoint. The adjunction on bounded-below etale-origin objects is exactly the natural Hom bijection of [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class]. Denote by $F_f$ the ordinary-etale compact-support functor, and by $P_f=Rf_!$ its pro-etale counterpart. The natural comparison of [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison] is $C_M:P_fV_XM\xrightarrow{\sim}V_YF_fM$. Transporting the etale counit along this Hom bijection characterizes the pro-etale counit on these objects by
$$\epsilon^{P}_{V_YH}=V_Y(\epsilon^{F}_H)\circ C_{f^\times H}$$
after the displayed right-adjoint identification. Indeed both counits are the inverse transposes of the identity of the same right-adjoint value. This also proves independence of the chosen antecedent, since the Hom bijection and $C$ are natural in its witness.

source.place: First paragraph: actual-adjoint and site comparisons, with the counit normalization made explicit

proof.text:
Apply [thm-asd-smooth-tensor] to the same $f$ and $A$. It gives an etale locally constant free rank-one sheaf $L$ with $W_f\cong L[2d]$ and an isomorphism
$$\phi_{f,H}:f^*H\otimes_A^LW_f\xrightarrow{\sim}f^\times H.$$
It specifies this very map as the transpose of the inverse projection formula followed by $1_H\otimes\epsilon^F_{A_Y}$ and the unit constraint. This statement supplies both the map and its isomorphy; an arbitrary isomorphism between these objects would not suffice. Its rank-one conclusion chooses no orientation $L\cong A_X(d)$.

source.place: First paragraph: the orientation-free tensor theorem and rank-one conclusion

proof.text:
The inverse of $L[2d]$ can be constructed without a new geometric theorem. Put $L^\vee=\mathcal Hom_A(L,A_X)$, using [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. On an etale cover trivializing $L$, evaluation $L\otimes_A L^\vee\to A_X$ is $A\otimes_A A\to A$, with inverse $a\mapsto1\otimes a$. These maps are compatible with restriction; the evaluations are isomorphisms by [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative], applied to underlying abelian sheaves. Tensoring by either line preserves injections: on the same cover it is tensoring by $A$, hence the original injection, and kernels vanish if their restrictions vanish. Thus both lines are flat. They are constructible because they are locally constant with finite rank-one stalks over the finite ring $A$. The tensor of these one-term flat complexes computes derived tensor; shifting the factors by $2d$ and $-2d$ cancels the shifts. Hence
$$W_f\otimes_A^L L^\vee[-2d]\cong A_X\cong L^\vee[-2d]\otimes_A^LW_f.$$
Apply the exact comparison $V_X$ and its monoidal isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. The two transported lines are still locally constant free rank one: pull back the same trivializing cover. They are flat by the same local injection argument. Consequently $M=V_XL^\vee[-2d]$ is bounded constructible and of finite Tor amplitude, and the two evaluations identify $\omega_f\otimes_A^LM$ and $M\otimes_A^L\omega_f$ with $A_X$. This is invertibility in precisely the sense of [def-pur-co-smoothness], including the required finite-Tor inverse.

source.place: First paragraph: “In particular it is tensor-invertible”; explicit dual line and evaluations

proof.text:
We identify the transported tensor map with the specified canonical map. The pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] and tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] identify
$$Lf^*K\otimes_A^L\omega_f\cong V_X(f^*H\otimes_A^LW_f).$$
Under these identifications, the projection formula for $P_f$ is the image of the etale one. To verify the map, use the chosen compactification from Step 1 and the definition [def-exchange-projection]. Its proper factor is the counit-defined projection map for $p$; apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence] to the commutative comparison square with vertical edges $p_{\mathrm{proet}},p_{\mathrm{et}}$ and horizontal edges $\nu_{\overline X},\nu_Y$. This lemma needs commutation of ringed topoi, not a Cartesian square. Use [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate] to identify the proper comparison with the very exchange mate occurring in this coherence lemma; properness supplies its quasi-compact and quasi-separated hypotheses. Thus the inverse of that mate, in the direction used by $C$, intertwines the two projection maps. For the open factor, [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison] identifies $V_{\overline X}j^{\mathrm{et}}_!$ with $j^{\mathrm{proet}}_!V_X$, termwise. Its compatibility with the canonical tensor map [lem-cbc-extension-zero-projection-formula] is checked before deriving. Compare the inverse tensor maps, whose common source after comparison is $j_!V_X(M\otimes j^{-1}Q)$: under the exact adjunction $j_!\dashv j^{-1}$ of [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero], both maps are the identity on $V_X(M\otimes j^{-1}Q)$, after the displayed pullback and tensor comparisons. They are equal by the adjunction bijection. Apply this equality to K-flat representatives and totalize to obtain equality of the derived maps. This is an equality proved by adjunction, not by testing derived morphisms on geometric stalks. Composing the proper and open identities gives the compact-support projection identity under $C$. With the counit identity of Step 2, the transpose of $V_X\phi_{f,H}$ is therefore
$$P_f(Lf^*K\otimes_A^L\omega_f)\xrightarrow{\mathrm{PF}^{-1}}K\otimes_A^LP_f\omega_f\xrightarrow{1\otimes\epsilon^P_{A_Y}}K.$$
Projection invertibility on these constructible finite-Tor inputs is [fix-prop-projection-formula]; using symmetry gives the order of factors displayed in [def-pur-co-smoothness]. That definition specifies $\theta_{f,K}$ by precisely this transpose. Injectivity of the adjunction Hom bijection [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] gives $V_X\phi_{f,H}=\theta_{f,K}$. Since a functor preserves an isomorphism, Step 3 proves clause 1 for the canonical map, naturally in $K$. The equality is equality of derived morphisms, obtained by adjunction, not a test of morphisms on stalks.

source.place: First paragraph: transporting the canonical tensor map, not merely its source and target; Stacks 07A4 and 0E48

proof.text:
For the Cartesian square in the statement, [lem-pur-smb-extraordinary] gives the canonical isomorphism
$$\beta_K:Lu^*Rf^!K\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf'^!Lv^*K.$$
Apply it at the constant coefficient object $K=A_Y$ (a one-term free, hence finite-Tor constructible object). Exact constant-coefficient inverse image sends $A_Y$ to $A_{Y'}$, giving $b:Lu^*\omega_f\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{f'}$. To check tensor-map compatibility, apply [prop-asd-smooth-base-change] to the antecedent $H$. Its statement gives the equality
$$\beta^{\mathrm{et}}_H\circ u^*\phi_{f,H}=\phi_{f',v^*H}\circ(1\otimes b^{\mathrm{et}}).$$
Realize this equality by $V_{X'}$. The pullback and tensor identifications are those of Step 5. Compact-support exchange is the transported etale exchange on witnessed bounded-below objects by [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale]. Step 2 identifies the counits and Hom bijections for $f$ and $f'$. Since exceptional exchange is their adjoint transpose, its realized map is exactly $\beta_K$: transposing gives $Lv^*\epsilon_f\circ\operatorname{Ex}_!^{-1}$ on both sides. Step 5 identifies both realized $\phi$'s with $\theta$'s, and the constant-object instance identifies the two $b$'s. The realized equality is therefore
$$\beta_K\circ Lu^*\theta_{f,K}=\theta_{f',Lv^*K}\circ(1\otimes b).$$
This proves the whole base-change clause for arbitrary $v$ in the fixed setting. No smoothness, flatness or properness of $v$ was used: the ordinary theorem allows any morphism of Noetherian schemes, and every corner here is finite type over $k$.

source.place: Second paragraph: arbitrary base change and compatibility with the tensor transformation

proof.text: Steps 4, 5 and 6 are exactly the three conditions of [def-pur-co-smoothness]. Thus for any composable smooth separated maps $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ$, both $f$ and $g$ are cohomologically smooth, by the preceding argument applied separately, and [lem-pur-co-smooth-composition] supplies cohomological smoothness of $gf$ and the dualizing-object isomorphism $\omega_{gf}\cong\omega_f\otimes_A^LLf^*\omega_g$. We now check the additional assertion about the canonical tensor transformations rather than taking that assertion from the lemma, whose statement only gives cohomological smoothness and the object isomorphism.

source.place: Second paragraph: all three conditions, then the dualizing-object formula for composition

proof.text:
Write $P_h=Rh_!$, $G_h=Rh^!$ and $W_h=\omega_h$ for $h=f,g,gf$. The canonical compact-support composition isomorphism of [thm-sf-comp-composition] and the natural Hom bijections of [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] identify $G_{gf}$ with $G_fG_g$: paste $\operatorname{Hom}(P_gP_fM,K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(P_fM,G_gK)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M,G_fG_gK)$. This is the adjunction-compatible composition comparison $c:G_{gf}\xrightarrow{\sim}G_fG_g$. By [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](2) its counit is $\epsilon_{g,K}\circ P_g(\epsilon_{f,G_gK})$. In particular put
$$q:Lf^*W_g\otimes_A^LW_f\xrightarrow{\theta_{f,W_g}}G_fW_g\xrightarrow{c_{A_Z}^{-1}}W_{gf}.$$
It is an isomorphism by Step 5 applied to $W_g$, which is finite-Tor constructible by Step 4. For any $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Z,A)$, the constructible typing and finite-Tor preservation explicitly stated in [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] give $G_gK\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$. Thus $\theta_{f,G_gK}$ is on its stated domain; the same is true of $\theta_{f,W_g}$ by Step 4. Compare $c_K\circ\theta_{gf,K}\circ(1\otimes q)$ with the composite
$$L(gf)^*K\otimes_A^LLf^*W_g\otimes_A^LW_f
\cong Lf^*(Lg^*K\otimes_A^LW_g)\otimes_A^LW_f
\xrightarrow{Lf^*\theta_{g,K}\otimes1}Lf^*G_gK\otimes_A^LW_f
\xrightarrow{\theta_{f,G_gK}}G_fG_gK.$$
All tensor identifications are the canonical ones of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Transpose each map successively through $P_f\dashv G_f$ and $P_g\dashv G_g$. Substitute the defining transpose of $\theta$ from [def-pur-co-smoothness]. Naturality of the projection map moves $\epsilon_{f,W_g}$ from the tensor factor into $P_f$; compatibility of projection with composition is exactly the associativity assertion of [fix-prop-projection-formula]. On both sides the resulting map is
$$P_gP_f\bigl(L(gf)^*K\otimes_A^LLf^*W_g\otimes_A^LW_f\bigr)
\xrightarrow{\mathrm{PF}_f^{-1}}P_g\bigl((Lg^*K\otimes_A^LW_g)\otimes_A^LP_fW_f\bigr)
\xrightarrow{P_g(1\otimes\epsilon_{f,A_Y})}P_g(Lg^*K\otimes_A^LW_g)
\xrightarrow{\mathrm{PF}_g^{-1}}K\otimes_A^LP_gW_g
\xrightarrow{1\otimes\epsilon_{g,A_Z}}K.$$
The counit equation for $c$ and the definition of $q$ give this same expression for the first map; the two individual tensor transposes give it for the second. Injectivity of the two Hom bijections proves the required equality. Symmetry replaces $Lf^*W_g\otimes W_f$ by $W_f\otimes Lf^*W_g$, giving the stated composition convention. This proves clause 4 without identifying any $W_h$ with a Tate twist.
